text:
Up to US$2 million per innovation, and the deadline has just been pushed back to 8 December.

Nexa Lighthouse is a Transition-to-Scale call from Grand Challenges Canada and AVPN, backed by funders including the Novo Nordisk Foundation, Bayer Foundation, India Health Fund, Sanofi Foundation and Temasek Foundation. It backs proven innovations across Asia and the Pacific that help health systems cope with climate-driven risks such as extreme heat, poor air quality, and mosquito-borne diseases like dengue and malaria.

Selected innovations receive roughly US$250,000 to US$2 million each, sized to how mature they are, along with support and access to a network of corporate and philanthropic funders across Asia.

You can apply if your organisation is incorporated and implementing in an eligible Asia-Pacific country, and your solution fits one of two themes: climate-informed early warning and monitoring, or climate-responsive patient care for these conditions. Untested ideas are not funded; this is money to scale something that already works.

The catch founders miss: the cut-off is 2:00 pm Eastern time, which is 12:30 am IST on 9 December, and proposals go only through GCC's Fluxx portal. Check the country list in the funding document before you start writing.

Last date: 8 December 2026

text:
Building something that creates jobs or skills? IIM Bangalore's NSRCEL will give you up to ₹12.5 lakh and take no equity for it.

Impact Orbit – Skilling and Livelihood Innovations is an impact-focused incubation track run by NSRCEL, the startup hub at IIM Bangalore, together with Capgemini. It is for ventures that build skills, create employment or improve livelihoods.

Selected ventures get grants of up to ₹12.5 lakh, one-on-one mentoring from domain experts, help sharpening their value proposition and getting ready to raise funds, and support with impact measurement and reporting. NSRCEL charges no fees and takes no equity.

This is not an idea-stage programme. You need a registered for-profit or not-for-profit entity with at least a year of operations, a proof of concept or completed pilots, early traction such as paying customers or users, at least one full-time founder and a team of three or more. Your model must contribute to at least three UN Sustainable Development Goals.

One practical tip: the official page says applications are "closing soon" but gives no closing date, so treat it as urgent. You apply through NSRCEL's Accubate form linked from the page, and it is a separate track from the AgeTech Impact Orbit call.

text:
Did you know the Tamil Nadu government runs its own SEBI-registered venture fund, writing cheques of ₹3–10 crore per round?

The Tamil Nadu Emerging Sector Seed Fund (TNESSF) is a Category I AIF managed by TNIFMC and sponsored by TIDCO and TIDEL, with a ₹100 crore anchor commitment. It invests in high-growth startups and MSMEs, mainly in emerging and sunrise sectors.

The typical investment is ₹3–10 crore per round in equity or convertible instruments. Early-stage companies can get up to ₹1 crore to reach their next milestone, and more mature companies may be able to raise larger amounts.

It is open to innovative, high-growth startups and MSMEs with revenue of up to ₹250 crore. The fund looks for a strong promoter track record, a capital-efficient model, clear economic and social impact for Tamil Nadu, credible exit potential and sound ESG practices.

The thing to remember: this is a venture fund, not a grant. It takes equity and runs normal VC-style due diligence, so go in with your data room, cap table and exit story ready. Applications are made through the "Apply" link on TNIFMC's website, which is linked from the TIDCO page.
